notes: FlatpanelsHD's launch coverage counts 13 speaker units in the bar, of which two fire upwards, plus two side-firing drivers and two beam tweeters; retailer spec sheets print the layout as 7.0.2 with Dolby Atmos, DTS:X and IMAX Enhanced. The subwoofer (SA-SW3/SA-SW5) and the rear speakers (SA-RS3S/SA-RS5) are wireless and sold separately, so the bar on its own has no bass module - shops often sell it bundled with one, and the bundle is the listing the bot will see.

Eleven speaker units, the same up-firing pair as the Bar 9 but without its passive radiators and beam tweeters; Stephanis prints the layout as 5.0.2. Wireless subwoofer and wireless rears are optional extras.

Nine drivers including two up-firing, sold as 5.0.2 on its own; the wireless 'Sub 7' bass module is a separate box, and the HTA7100KIT that Cypriot shops list is the bar plus that subwoofer, printed as 5.1.2. Reviews are split on the bar's tuning (Tom's Guide recommends it, TechRadar faults the lack of EQ control), so read the Reviews column before buying.

3.1.2 with six speaker units: three front-firing with a dedicated centre, two up-firing for the height channels, and a wireless subwoofer in the box. Dolby Atmos and DTS:X. The cheapest Sony with real up-firing drivers and a sub included.

The 2021 flagship, still stocked in Cyprus and Greece and printed as 7.1.2 by the shops: two up-firing drivers, two beam tweeters, optional SA-SW3/SW5 wireless subwoofer and SA-RS3S/RS5 wireless rears. Kept on the list because it is routinely discounted below the Bar 8 that replaced it; the layout here follows the retailer listings rather than a current Sony spec page.
